title: What is left of the triangle at Step three?
description: The Ruhee Triangle starts with area one square unit. The video counts the remaining triangles, the holes and the remaining area at Step three. Keeko's doubt is that a quarter is taken away at each step, so one quarter is left.
teaching_notes: One idea: each step keeps three of the four equal parts of every triangle, so the count is multiplied by three and the area by three quarters. Watch for students who subtract a quarter at every step.

source: For the Sierpinski Triangle with starting area 1 square unit
video_script.why: The child knows how the Ruhee Triangle is cut and now counts what is left after three rounds.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the triangles by three each step, add the new holes to the old ones, and multiply the area by three quarters each step.
video_script.anchor: the Ruhee Triangle of the book, drawn up to Step three, with a starting area of one square unit
video_script.wrong_answer: one quarter of the area is left
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes away one quarter at each of the three steps and says one quarter of the area is left. Each step removes a quarter of what is left, so three quarters stay each time and the area is multiplied by three quarters.
video_script.payoff_line: Step three leaves twenty seven triangles, thirteen holes and twenty seven over sixty four of a square unit

final_answer.value: 27 triangles, 13 holes and 27/64 square unit of area
final_answer.spoken: twenty seven triangles, thirteen holes and twenty seven over sixty four of a square unit

video_script.fraction_reading: 27/64 is read twenty seven over sixty four

names.Ruhee: Polish mathematician who discovered the carpet and the triangle

hold_back: Answer: 27 triangles, 13 holes and 27/64 square unit of area
maths_rules: each remaining triangle gives 3 triangles at the next step
each remaining triangle makes one new hole and old holes stay
each step keeps 3 of the 4 equal parts, so the area is multiplied by 3/4
Step 3 area: 3/4 x 3/4 x 3/4 = 27/64 square unit
video_script.design: The triangle is drawn to Step three on the stage; a small table of counts grows beside it as each step is worked.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the Ruhee Triangle at Step 3; a note: starting area 1 square unit

marks.book: the title card and the triangle at Step 3 appear
marks.area: the starting area is written beside the triangle
marks.ask: three question marks appear: triangles, holes, area

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the Ruhee Triangle.
<bookmark mark='area'/>The first triangle has an area of one square unit.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>At Step three, how many triangles remain, how many holes appear, and how much area is left?

beats.on_screen: the triangle stays on the board with the three question marks underlined

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one triangle is cut into 4 equal triangles by joining midpoints; the middle one is shaded out, 3 remain

marks.cut: one triangle is cut into four equal triangles
marks.hole: the middle triangle fades and leaves a gap

narration: <bookmark mark='cut'/>Every step cuts each remaining triangle into four equal triangles.
<bookmark mark='hole'/>The middle one is removed. The gap it leaves is a hole.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Three of the four parts stay, so each triangle gives three triangles and one new hole.

beats.on_screen: Given: starting area 1 square unit. Each step keeps 3 of the 4 equal parts of every triangle.

marks.given: the starting area and the rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the starting area is one square unit. Each step keeps three of the four equal parts of every triangle.

beats.on_screen: To find: remaining triangles, holes and area at Step 3

marks.find: the words triangles, holes and area at Step 3 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remaining triangles, the holes and the area at Step three.

beats.on_screen: Triangles: 1 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 3 x 3 x 3 = 27

marks.rule: the line each step multiplies the triangles by 3 is written
marks.calc: 3 x 3 x 3 = 27 is written under the Step 3 triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, count the triangles. Each step multiplies the triangles by three, and there are three steps.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Three times three times three is twenty seven triangles.

beats.on_screen: Holes: Step 1 has 1, Step 2 adds 3, Step 3 adds 9, so 1 + 3 + 9 = 13

marks.rule: the line each remaining triangle makes one new hole, old holes stay is written
marks.calc: 1 + 3 + 9 = 13 is written under the Step 3 triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, count the holes. Each remaining triangle makes one new hole, and the old holes stay.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Step one has one hole, Step two adds three, and Step three adds nine. One plus three plus nine is thirteen holes.

beats.on_screen: Area: each step keeps 3/4, so 3/4 x 3/4 x 3/4 = 27/64 square unit

marks.rule: the line each step multiplies the area by 3/4 is written
marks.calc: 3/4 x 3/4 x 3/4 = 27/64 is written under the Step 3 triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, find the area. Each step keeps three quarters of the area, so we multiply by three quarters three times.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Three quarters times three quarters times three quarters is twenty seven over sixty four of a square unit.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 27 triangles, 13 holes and 27/64 square unit of area
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Step three leaves twenty seven triangles, thirteen holes and twenty seven over sixty four of a square unit.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the triangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 1/4 taken away three times, struck through; the Step 2 triangle shows a quarter of the remaining area shaded out

marks.doubt: the bubble with a quarter taken away three times appears
marks.look: at Step 2 only a quarter of the remaining area is shaded out, not of the whole
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the line multiply by 3/4 returns

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one quarter of the area is left. A quarter is taken away at each of three steps.
<bookmark mark='look'/>Look at Step two. A quarter is taken from what is left, and that is less than a quarter of the whole.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Three quarters stay each time, so we multiply by three quarters.
